Define a shared environmental-space lattice

Source: R/espace.R
dn_space.Rd

Builds the common R x R lattice on which all species niches and all region climate availabilities are estimated, from the global distribution of environmental scores (typically the first two principal components of climate over all terrestrial cells).

Usage

dn_space(scores, R = 100L, clip_q = c(0.001, 0.999), bw_frac = 0.02)

Arguments

scores

numeric matrix (n x 2) of environmental scores for the global background (all terrestrial grid cells), not for any one species or region. The lattice must be shared or no two densities are comparable.

R

lattice resolution per axis (default 100, as calibrated in the source studies; sensitivity there: Spearman >= 0.996 across 60-150).

clip_q

lower/upper quantiles at which the axes are clipped before 5% padding (default c(0.001, 0.999)).

bw_frac

fixed kernel bandwidth as a fraction of the axis range (default 0.02; one bandwidth for every object so that estimated niche breadth reflects ecology, not sample size).

Value

an object of class dn_space: list with x_edges, y_edges, R, bw_cells.

Examples

set.seed(1)
bg <- cbind(rnorm(5000), rnorm(5000))   # global background scores
sp <- dn_space(bg, R = 60)
sp
#> <dn_space> 60 x 60 lattice, bandwidth 1.20 cells
#>   PC1 [-3.508, 3.225]  PC2 [-3.425, 3.302]
